exercises.name: Back Extension (Hyperextension)

source_english.description: A Back Extension (Hyperextension) uses a supported hip hinge: the torso lowers from the hips and returns only to a neutral line.
instructions: Set the machine so the hips are supported and the feet or legs are secured.
Hinge forward from the hips with a neutral spine and keep the head aligned.
Raise the torso until it is in line with the legs by squeezing the glutes.
Pause briefly, then lower under control without rounding deeply.
form_cues: Move at the hips.
Finish neutral, not hyperextended.
Keep the neck relaxed.
common_mistakes: Using the arms to create momentum.
source_english.safety_note: Stop at a neutral torso line; do not force the machine or bench into hyperextension.

source_english.description: A machine hip thrust uses the back and hip pads to support the body while the machine resistance follows a glute-driven hip-extension path.
instructions: Adjust the machine so the back and hip pads support you comfortably with both feet flat.
Set the resistance, brace your core, and position the belt or pad securely across the hips.
Drive through both feet to extend the hips until the torso and thighs align.
Pause briefly, then lower the hips under control to the starting position.
form_cues: Keep the feet planted and knees tracking over the toes.
Brace before each repetition.
Stop at a straight torso-to-thigh line.
common_mistakes: Starting with the hips too far forward or back on the pad.
Pushing with the toes instead of the whole foot.
source_english.safety_note: Check the pad, belt, and machine settings before loading resistance.

source_english.description: A machine squat uses shoulder pads and a guided track to lower the hips and press the carriage upward.
instructions: Adjust the shoulder pads and foot platform so the knees are comfortably bent at the start.
Brace against the support and place both feet evenly on the platform.
Lower into the squat by bending the hips and knees while keeping the feet planted.
Press through the feet to return without locking the knees.
form_cues: Keep the back against the pad.
Track both knees with the toes.
Control the machine through the full range.
common_mistakes: Letting the hips lift from the pad.
